title: Explore a Real GitHub Repository
description: No installation needed today. Visit the GitHub repository for freeCodeCamp — one of the most starred open-source projects in the world — and explore it like a developer would.
steps: Find and note the total number of commits shown on the repository page
Click the 'commits' link and read the last 3 commit messages
Look at the repository's README.md and identify what the project is about
Find the 'Issues' tab and note roughly how many open issues there are
Find the 'Branches' section and note how many branches exist
expected_output: A short note (even just mental notes) of what you found — number of commits, what the last 3 commits changed, and what the project does.
tips: The commit count is shown near the top of the file list, often as '12,345 commits'
Each commit message tells you what changed — good commit messages are short and descriptive
The README is the front page of every repository — always read it first
